1.why: Reset tokens are stored with sessionId and /api/reset-verify plus validOwnedToken reject tokens that do not match the caller session.

2.why: A token from another session fails the record.sessionId !== session.id check, so the same code does not work for any other user/session.

3.why: Password reset only marks the token used and updates mockAccount.passwordHash; other entries in the sessions Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Primary server is Bun.serve with TLS cert/key and HTTP is redirected to HTTPS, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and MFA material are kept/returned in plaintext rather than encrypted at rest.

6.why: There is no real email channel; the simulated delivery path exposes the raw reset token (and later MFA code) in the client logs UI.

7.why: Identifiers are strict-regex cleaned, passwords validated server-side, JSON bodies parsed safely, and DOM updates use textContent rather than unescaped HTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded HTTP→HTTPS localhost redirect with no user-controlled redirect parameters.

9.why: No email templates render user input as HTML/scripts; simulation output is written via textContent.

10.why: API responses include testToken and mfaCode, and the Logs panel deliberately prints those secrets to the page.

11.why: Runtime passwords use Bun bcrypt, but the MFA secret "482913" is hardcoded in the source and returned to the client.

12.why: The documented demo-account identifier plus fixed MFA code 482913 act as default/training credentials.

13.why: tooMany rate limits apply to reset-request (3), reset-verify (5), and mfa-verify (5), with additional per-token verifyAttempts capping.

14.why: Message text is generic, but testToken is only present when identifier === "demo-account", which reveals account existence.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues values (base64url), single-use, time-limited, and bound to the requesting session.
